etymology: Latin: onus probandi. The burden sits with whoever makes the claim - and the shift is the act of handing it over.
committed_when: A claim has been made with no evidence offered.
tell: The reply is “prove me wrong” or “do your own research”, and the original claim is never defended.
counter: State who holds the burden and what would count as evidence. A claim does not become true by surviving an audit it never had to pass.
senses: Demanding that others disprove a claim instead of supporting it, so that the absence of disproof is treated as support.
It works because a demand sounds like an invitation to debate. The audience rarely notices that the person making the claim has not made a case for it.
example: “Show me the study that says it is harmful.” The claim was that it is safe; the absent study is not a finding.

confused_with.tell: Ignorance treats a gap as proof; the shift assigns the work of closing the gap to the sceptic.
